## 1. Route supplies through a puzzle village

Implement allocate(stock, requests). stock maps names to nonnegative integer quantities. Each request is an (item, quantity) pair with a positive integer quantity. Process requests in order. Accept only when the full quantity is available; otherwise reject without changing stock. Unknown items are rejected. Return (remaining, decisions): a new stock dictionary and a list of booleans. Do not mutate either input. Treat valid quantities as preconditions.

Predict an ordinary result before coding. Start with the smallest part you can
run and inspect. Use Colab for notebooks and the local workspace introduced in
the units for packaging or command-line tasks.

## 2. Set up the experiment

```python
def allocate(stock, requests):
    """Return independent remaining stock and one decision per request."""
    # Implement the allocation contract.
    pass
```

The starter is deliberately incomplete. Implement the contract; do not change
the expected results to match an incorrect implementation.

## 3. Check the observable results

1. For {"rope": 3, "lamp": 1} and [("rope", 2), ("rope", 2), ("lamp", 1)], return ({"rope": 1, "lamp": 0}, [True, False, True]).
2. Empty requests return an equal but independent stock dictionary and an empty decisions list.
3. An unknown item is rejected without adding a stock entry.
4. After the call, the original stock is unchanged. Mutating remaining must not alter it. Explain why a shallow copy is sufficient for integer values.

Record actual outputs beside predictions. Reduce a failure to a small example,
change one cause at a time, and repeat the failed check after repairing it.

## 4. Change one condition

Change one rope request to quantity 1, reverse the two rope requests, and trace the decisions. Explain why order is part of the contract.
